test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 26 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Magnification produced by a spherical mirror is equal to:

options.text: height of an image - height of an object
frac {(height of an image)} {(height of an object)}
height of an object - height of an image
frac {(height of an object)} {(height of an image )}

solution:
The correct answer is ** frac {(height of an image)} {(height of an object)}**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **enlargement of the picture **created by **spherical mirrors** in relation to the size of the object is known as **magnification.**
 
• It is represented by the **symbol m** and represents the **height of the image in relation to the height of the object.**
 
• A **spherical mirror's magnification (m) **can be represented as follows:
 
 
• **m = h′ / h, **where **h′** is the **image's height** and** h** is the **object's height.**
 
 
 
• Additionally, it is **equivalent to** the **opposite of the image distance (v)** to **object distance ratio (u)**.
 
 
• **m** = **−v / u**
 
 
 
• Convention dictates that the **distance between objects** is always **negative**. When a mirror is used,** real images** are created in** front of the mirror**, and **virtual images** are created **behind the mirror**.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is: frac {(height of an image)} {(height of an object)}

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Our ability to judge the** size of the produced picture** in relation to the object is **aided by magnification.** It explains whether the image created when an object is placed at various places on the **primary axis** is magnified, decreased, or equal to the object.
 
• The **magnification** that is** positive **denotes a** virtual and erect image.**
 
• The** real and inverted image** is shown by a** negative magnification** magnitude.
